title_en: Guiding Case No. 231: Dongguan FengMou Shipping Co., Ltd. v. Dongying XinMou Logistics Co., Ltd. — dispute over maritime salvage
ruling_gist_en: Salvage operations between ships belonging to the same shipowner: the ship providing salvage services shall be regarded as an independent salvor. Where there is no circumstance as provided in Article 187 of the Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China with respect to the salving ship, the salvage payment obtained by it in accordance with Article 191 of the Maritime Law shall not be cancelled or reduced due to the negligence of the ship in distress which is owned by the same shipowner.

full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 231

Dongguan Fengmou Shipping Co., Ltd. v. Dongying Xinmou Logistics Co., Ltd. — dispute over maritime salvage

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and released on November 25, 2024)

Keywords
civil; maritime salvage; salvage reward; same shipowner

Ruling Gist

Where salvage is performed between vessels belonging to the same shipowner, the vessel participating in the salvage shall be deemed an independent salvor. Where the salving vessel does not fall under any circumstance specified in Article 187 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, the salvage reward obtained by it under Article 191 of the Maritime Code shall not be disallowed or reduced on account of the fault of the vessel in distress that belongs to the same shipowner.

Basic Facts

On January 1, 2016, Dongying Xinmou Logistics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter “Dongying Xinmou Logistics”) entered into a storage agreement with Shandong Wanmou Group Dongying Port Navigation Co., Ltd., under which Dongying Xinmou Logistics leased two oil tanks with numbers V-6105 and V-6106.

The vessels “Mousheng Oil 9” and “Mousheng Oil 16” were both owned by Dongguan Fengmou Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter “Dongguan Fengmou Shipping”). On January 10, 2017, “Mousheng Oil 16” loaded 6,500 tons of gasoline from oil tank V-6106 of Shandong Wanmou Group Dongying Port Navigation Co., Ltd. On January 16, 2017, while conducting gasoline loading operations at berth No. 16 of the South Harbor Basin of Dongying Port, “Mousheng Oil 16” experienced a gasoline leakage into the pump room and engine room due to a gap in the transverse bulkhead between the engine room and the pump room, as well as faults in personnel management and operation, creating a major hazard endangering personnel, the vessel, and port safety. During a patrol, law enforcement officers of the Dongying Maritime Safety Office discovered the situation and reported it to the Dongying Municipal Maritime Search and Rescue Center. The local government established an emergency response task force for the “Mousheng Oil 16” incident. Pursuant to the arrangements and requirements of the Dongying Municipal Maritime Search and Rescue Center and the emergency response task force, multiple entities, including Dongguan Fengmou Shipping, participated in the rescue and salvage operations. On January 19, 2017, Dongguan Fengmou Shipping dispatched “Mousheng Oil 9” to enter the port to participate in the salvage. At approximately 19:00 on January 22, all gasoline loaded on “Mousheng Oil 16” was transferred to “Mousheng Oil 9.” By noon on February 7, after cleaning, degassing, and ventilation of the pump room and engine room of “Mousheng Oil 16,” oxygen and explosion levels returned to normal, and the hazard was eliminated.

Dongguan Fengmou Shipping filed a lawsuit with the Qingdao Maritime Court, requesting a judgment ordering Dongying Xinmou Logistics (the owner of the loaded gasoline) to pay a salvage reward, corresponding interest, and bear the litigation costs. During the proceedings, Dongying Xinmou Logistics argued that “Mousheng Oil 16” was at fault for the incident in question; that both “Mousheng Oil 16” and “Mousheng Oil 9” were owned by Dongguan Fengmou Shipping; and that under Article 187 of the Maritime Code, Dongguan Fengmou Shipping’s salvage reward should be disallowed or reduced due to its own fault.

Separately, after the hazard was eliminated, other entities that participated in the rescue and salvage operations filed a lawsuit with the Qingdao Maritime Court against Dongying Xinmou Logistics and Dongguan Fengmou Shipping for a salvage reward. On November 19, 2020, Dongying Xinmou Logistics and the other participating entities reached a settlement agreement during the enforcement proceedings before the Qingdao Maritime Court, pursuant to which Dongying Xinmou Logistics paid the salvage reward and corresponding interest.

Judgment

The Qingdao Maritime Court rendered a civil judgment (2019) Lu 72 Min Chu No. 137 on September 26, 2019, dismissing all claims of Dongguan Fengmou Shipping Co., Ltd. After the first-instance judgment was announced, Dongguan Fengmou Shipping Co., Ltd. appealed. The Shandong High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2020) Lu Min Zhong No. 14 on March 16, 2020: 1. Reversing the civil judgment (2019) Lu 72 Min Chu No. 137 of the Qingdao Maritime Court; 2. Ordering Dongying Xinmou Logistics Co., Ltd. to pay Dongguan Fengmou Shipping Co., Ltd. a salvage reward of RMB 1,290,384 and corresponding interest within ten days from the effective date of this judgment; 3. Dismissing the other claims of Dongguan Fengmou Shipping Co., Ltd. After the second-instance judgment was announced, Dongying Xinmou Logistics Co., Ltd. applied for retrial. The Supreme People's Court rendered a civil ruling (2020) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 4813 on November 23, 2020, rejecting the retrial application of Dongying Xinmou Logistics Co., Ltd.

Reasoning

To encourage vessels belonging to the same shipowner to participate in maritime salvage, to avoid unfairly depriving the crew participating in the salvage of the salvage reward they deserve, and to fairly protect the interests of the insurers of each vessel, Article 191 of the Maritime Code provides: “Salvage operations performed between vessels of the same owner shall be subject to the provisions of this Chapter with respect to the right of the salvor to obtain salvage payment.” This provision establishes that salvage between vessels owned by the same civil subject may also give rise to a claim for salvage payment. Article 187 of the Maritime Code provides: “If the salvage operation becomes necessary or more difficult due to the fault of the salvor, or if the salvor has committed fraud or other dishonest conduct, the salvage payment payable to the salvor shall be disallowed or reduced.” This provision sets out the circumstances under which salvage payment in maritime salvage may be disallowed or reduced.

Under China’s litigation system, a lawsuit may not be brought in the name of a vessel. However, when determining the amount of salvage reward, the salving vessel may be treated as an independent unit. Where the incident giving rise to the salvage is caused by improper navigation or cargo handling on the part of the vessel in distress, the salving vessel’s claim for salvage reward, where the salving vessel belongs to the same owner as the vessel in distress, shall not be affected. The fault and liability of the two vessels in the salvage relationship shall not be conflated merely because they belong to the same owner. A fault in navigation or cargo handling on the part of the vessel in distress that gives rise to a maritime casualty shall not be deemed the fault of the salving vessel. The term “salvor” in Article 187 of the Maritime Code shall be understood to refer to the salving vessel, not the owner of the salving vessel. As long as the salving vessel does not fall under any circumstance specified in Article 187 of the Maritime Code, the salvage reward obtained by it shall not be disallowed or reduced.

In this case, although “Mousheng Oil 16” and “Mousheng Oil 9” belonged to the same shipowner, “Mousheng Oil 9,” as the salving vessel, was not at fault for the occurrence of the maritime casualty in question. Dongying Xinmou Logistics also failed to adduce evidence that “Mousheng Oil 9” committed fraud or other dishonest conduct during the salvage operation. Therefore, the salvage reward for “Mousheng Oil 9” shall not be disallowed or reduced on account of the fault of “Mousheng Oil 16” in the maritime casualty.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 187 and Article 191 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China
